---
title: "Perception and Observation Trust"
unit_id: "unit-10"

## Four Reports About One Patch

The repository change now reaches a controller that operates a low-energy lab
gantry. The patch adjusts how the gantry slows near the end of its rail. Before
the change can run, the team asks a seemingly simple question: did the intended
controller reach the test and deployment environments?

Four reports arrive.

The file-system monitor says the controller source has the new hash. The test
runner says the patched controller passed its simulation suite. A reviewer
opens the generated report and confirms the same passing results. The
deployment observer, however, says the running service still exposes the old
controller identity.

Three reports appear to support the patch and one contradicts them. A majority
vote would accept the change. That would be a mistake.

The test runner and reviewer both read artifacts produced from the same stale
build cache. They are two reports but one causal source. The file-system monitor
proves that a file exists at a particular location and revision, not that the
build consumed it. The deployment observer may be stale too; its last sample
could predate the rollout. None of the four reports is direct access to reality.
Each is a measurement transformed by an instrument, clock, calibration,
software path, model, and interpretation.

This is perception in its broadest systems sense. Cameras, microphones, force
sensors, logs, test runners, reviewers, APIs, and deployment probes all turn
parts of the world into claims that another component may use. Their outputs
can be useful without being true in every respect. They can agree because they
are independent, because they share a cause, or because they share a mistake.
They can disagree because one is wrong, because they observed different times,
or because each measured a different property.

An advanced AI stack cannot begin with “the sensor saw it” or “the tool
reported success.” It needs to know which observation occurred, through which
path, at what time, under which conditions, with which dependencies, and for
which decision. Observation trust is not a permanent score attached to a
source. It is a bounded permission to use a particular report for a particular
purpose while preserving what remains uncertain.

The gantry makes the stakes visible. A stale build report may waste a release.
A stale position estimate can turn the same motor command from admissible to
dangerous. The discipline is continuous across those cases, but the permitted
latency and residual risk are not. As effects become faster and less
reversible, the observation contract must become narrower.

## A Report Is Not the World

Every observation has at least three identities: the thing being observed, the
instrument or process that produced the measurement, and the transformation
that converted the measurement into a usable hypothesis.

For the file-system report, the object is a path at a repository revision. The
instrument is a file reader running in an environment. The transformation may
be a hash function and a rule saying which hash denotes the candidate. For the
test report, the object is not simply “the patch.” It is a build artifact,
fixture set, simulator version, selected tests, environment, and execution. The
reviewer's observation includes the report generation path and whatever source
the reviewer actually inspected. The deployment probe has an endpoint,
credential, sampling time, routing path, and rule for identifying the running
controller.

Those details do not prove any report correct. They establish what the report
could mean. Without them, later consumers cannot distinguish a current
observation from a cached one, an independent measurement from a repeated
summary, or a claim about source code from a claim about deployed behavior.

This is why provenance is necessary but insufficient. Provenance can show that
a report came from the expected process. The expected process can still be
miscalibrated, observe the wrong target, share a hidden dependency, or produce
an answer outside its competence. A signed test result from the wrong build is
authentically wrong.

An observation record therefore carries identity and limits together. It names
the variables requested by the consumer, the channels used, timestamps and
clock model, calibration and pose where relevant, preprocessing and model
versions, coverage and missingness, per-channel hypotheses, uncertainty,
dependence assumptions, disagreement, freshness, permitted consumers,
authority, cost, and residuals. The record should be small enough to use but
specific enough to invalidate.

The last property matters. If the build cache changes, the test observation may
need to be rerun. If a camera moves, its old geometric calibration cannot
silently follow. If a deployment probe changes endpoint or credential, its
prior observation does not remain current by name alone. An observation that
cannot say what would make it stale is not a durable input to consequential
reasoning.

## Observation Is Task-Relative

The question “is this report trustworthy?” is usually underspecified.
Trustworthy for what?

The file-system hash may be adequate to prove that a source file was written.
It is inadequate to prove that the test runner compiled that file. The
simulation report may support a bounded claim about selected trajectories in a
particular simulator. It is inadequate to prove that the physical gantry uses
the candidate or that the real stopping distance improved. A deployment probe
may identify the running artifact while saying nothing about the actuator,
sensor, payload, or rail condition.

An observation need begins with the consumer's decision. It names the variables
required, consequence class, deadline, acceptable uncertainty, coverage, and
maximum authority. A documentation suggestion can tolerate older repository
state than a merge decision. A reversible simulation can tolerate more
uncertainty than a command that moves mass near a person. The same report can
be admissible for one use and rejected for another without contradiction.

This task-relative boundary prevents confidence from becoming authority. A
detector may be highly confident that an object is present; that does not grant
permission to move toward it. A deployment probe may be certain which binary is
running; that does not establish that the binary is safe. The observation layer
supplies bounded evidence. Governance and control decide whether that evidence
is sufficient for a proposed effect.

The boundary also makes abstention meaningful. “Unknown” is not failure to
produce a polished answer. It is the correct result when the available channels
cannot satisfy the observation need. The system can request a fresh sample,
change viewpoint, inspect another artifact, ask a person, reduce the action, or
enter a safe hold. A useful perception system knows when additional sensing is
worth its time, energy, privacy cost, and physical risk.

## Agreement Is Not Independence

Return to the test runner and reviewer. They agree because the reviewer reads
the test runner's generated report. Counting them as two pieces of evidence
would be obvious double counting. The harder cases are less visible.

Two cameras can share glare, weather, power, clock drift, or a calibration
service. A camera and lidar can have different device identities while sharing
an incorrect pose transform. Two software agents can call different tools that
read the same cache. Two human reviewers can rely on the same generated
summary. Several models can inherit one training-set blind spot. Distinct
channels do not imply distinct causes.

The observation record therefore retains a dependence graph or, at minimum,
declared common-cause groups. Agreeing channels with one known root should not
be promoted as if they were independent confirmations. Disagreeing channels
should not be averaged into a confident middle merely because fusion software
requires one output.

The current formal work behind this chapter proves a narrow version of that
rule. In a finite authored pair model, two usable agreeing records with the same
declared dependence root count as one independent evidence item. Distinct
declared roots count as two inside that model, and disagreement remains
disagreement. The lifecycle preserves exact observation, channel,
calibration, clock, pose, dependence, hypothesis, consumer, residual, and
version identities while rejecting stale or inflated handoffs.

But even distinct declared roots are not enough. Camera and lidar can have
separate device roots while sharing a scene obstruction or synchronization
fault. The formal counterexample shows that the same pairwise summary can
correspond to opposite global common-cause states. No classifier that sees only
the pair labels can always recover the larger causal graph.

That limitation is the useful result. The proof does not discover real causal
dependence. It establishes why a consumer must not treat two labels as a
universal guarantee of independence. Common-cause context, its version and
expiry, and unresolved uncertainty must travel with the fused observation.

For the gantry patch, the correct fusion is not “three votes to one.” It is
closer to this: source file updated; test and review jointly support one stale
build artifact; deployment identity conflicts with the intended candidate;
current physical-controller identity unknown. That representation is less
decisive and far more useful.

## Calibration and Missingness Travel With the Result

A confidence number is meaningful only under the conditions that gave it a
relationship to outcomes. Calibration on one repository family, sensor suite,
location, weather regime, payload, or population does not automatically survive
a change in any of them.

Suppose the clean-build test runner historically reports ninety percent
confidence when nine of ten similarly scored patches later pass independent
review. That relationship can break when the test selector changes, a new
language enters the repository, generated tests dominate the suite, or the
review process begins reading the runner's own explanations. The number remains
well formed while its empirical meaning decays.

Physical perception adds more ways to drift. A camera can move. A lens can
foul. Temperature can alter a sensor. A new payload can change vibration and
braking. A model update can preserve clean accuracy while changing confidence
under glare or occlusion. Calibration should therefore carry its cohort,
environment, instrument and model versions, collection period, uncertainty,
expiry conditions, and the consumers for which it was evaluated.

Missingness must remain visible for the same reason. If lidar drops out in
rain, the remaining camera is not simply a smaller version of the normal sensor
suite. The missing channel may be informative about the operating condition,
and the fusion model may never have been qualified for that pattern. A clear
camera view of the near rail does not cover the occluded far rail. A passing
unit-test subset does not cover the skipped integration test.

The observation record should preserve which channels were expected, present,
late, corrupted, rejected, or never queried. It should say whether the fusion
route was trained and calibrated for that pattern and whether uncertainty rose
appropriately. Imputation can support a bounded decision, but it cannot rewrite
an absent measurement as an observed one.

This discipline also protects disagreement. A high fused score can coexist
with one channel warning about a rare, consequential state. Consumers may need
the fused estimate, the per-channel hypotheses, and the missingness pattern
together. The point is not to force every downstream component to process raw
sensor streams. It is to keep the information that determines whether the
summary is fit for the proposed decision.

## Disagreement Is a Routing Signal

Fusion systems are often rewarded for producing one answer. Consequential
systems sometimes need to preserve several.

The deployment contradiction can arise from at least four hypotheses. The
rollout never occurred. The deployment probe sampled before the rollout. The
probe reached a different replica. Or the build itself used stale input. Each
hypothesis suggests a different next observation.

The system can query the deployment manifest by immutable digest, bypass the
build cache, sample every replica, compare the running controller's self-report
with an external artifact measurement, and rerun the simulation from the
content-addressed candidate. These actions are *active observation*: the
system chooses another measurement because its expected decision value exceeds
the cost.

Active observation is not free. A new camera view can move a robot or expose a
person. A diagnostic query can consume credentials, reveal data, delay a
deadline, or perturb the system being measured. Rebuilding from scratch costs
compute and time. Asking a human consumes attention. The sensing action needs
its own authority and budget; uncertainty does not authorize unlimited
inspection.

This produces a practical routing rule. Fresh, adequately covered, calibrated,
and sufficiently independent evidence may support the named decision. Stale,
contradictory, unsupported, or undercovered evidence routes to a fresh sample,
alternative channel, narrower action, human review, abstention, degraded mode,
or safe hold. The system should record which branch it took and why.

Safe hold is a route, not a safety claim. It may be unreachable, too slow, or
harmful in a particular environment. Its adequacy must be tested separately.
The observation layer can identify that its own evidence is insufficient; it
cannot prove that every downstream fallback will work.

## Freshness Is Part of Meaning

Some observations decay slowly. Others expire between sensing and action.

A repository license record may remain useful for months if the dependency does
not change. A deployment identity can become stale during a rollout. A gantry
position estimate may be unusable milliseconds later. Freshness is therefore
not one global time-to-live. It belongs to the variable, dynamics, consumer,
consequence, and action horizon.

Suppose the gantry controller receives a move command at tick five. The plant
lease expires at tick eight. Its state was observed at tick four, with maximum
permitted age two. Worst-case sensing, estimation, scheduling, and control
latency must still fit inside the control period. The estimated state interval
must lie inside the declared envelope, requested force and motion must remain
within actuator limits, and the stopping-distance bound must fit inside the
remaining margin.

The symbolic command can remain identical while those conditions change. If
latency grows beyond the period or stopping margin shrinks below the bound, the
advanced command becomes inadmissible. A correct plan executed late can be the
wrong action.

This is where observation trust becomes physical control. The controller does
not consume “position equals five” as timeless truth. It consumes a
time-stamped estimate, uncertainty interval, estimator identity, plant model,
clock, and age. Every control period rechecks whether that packet still supports
the command. Missing sensing, clock disagreement, stale human-presence state,
or lost stopping margin narrows authority toward a baseline controller, hold,
or independent stop.

The learned or deliberative controller cannot vote itself more time. Its
confidence does not extend the lease. Urgency does not convert missing evidence
into permission.

## From Observation to Physical Effect

A language model can propose a trajectory or explain why a move seems safe. A
real-time controller must satisfy a different contract.

The physical-control lease binds the exact plant and payload, workspace,
maintenance state, estimator and dynamics model, control period, latency and
jitter budgets, force, speed, energy, space and contact limits, human-presence
mode, advanced controller, baseline controller, switching monitor, interlocks,
stop path, exploration authority, effect observations, compensation duties,
irreversible residuals, and expiry.

These fields separate timescales and authorities. A slower model may propose a
goal or recovery option. A local controller closes the fast loop. An
independent monitor can filter, switch, hold, isolate, or stop. A mechanically
simple interlock may own the fastest boundary. The slower component does not
inherit the deadline or trust of the faster one.

Control-barrier methods, constrained learning, and advanced-plus-baseline
switching architectures provide strong ways to construct parts of this system.
Their guarantees remain conditional. A barrier depends on its model, state
estimate, safe set, feasibility, and timing. A baseline controller may share
the failed sensor, power supply, or runtime. Switching can happen too late or
oscillate. An emergency stop can leave residual energy or an unstable load.

The architecture does not solve those engineering problems by naming them. It
prevents a general AI capability claim from erasing them. A controller remains
qualified only for a plant-specific operating envelope whose assumptions and
fallback reachability are current.

For the gantry, the patch cannot move from clean simulation to physical action
because three reports looked favorable. The system must establish the running
controller identity, rerun the candidate from current inputs, verify the state
and timing envelope, confirm the independent stop path, and begin in a
physically isolated low-energy setting. Human proximity is a separate evidence
and authority lane.

## Simulation Is an Instrument, Not a World

The simulation report is still valuable. It can exercise thousands of
trajectories, seed deadline misses, vary payloads, expose saturation, and test
fallback branches that would be irresponsible to discover first on hardware.
It is a development and falsification instrument.

Its limits must be explicit. A simulator chooses dynamics, contact, friction,
latency, sensor noise, human behavior, fault distributions, and omitted
phenomena. A controller can exploit those choices. A digital twin can stay
synchronized with a particular plant and fuse telemetry, maintenance history,
and learned residuals, yet remain a model with a validity envelope rather than
a more convenient reality.

A twin or simulator record should name plant identity, geometry and dynamics
version, synchronization delay, represented and omitted phenomena, operating
region, validation episodes, fault library, uncertainty, sim-to-real
residuals, expiry, and permitted consumers. Predicted and observed trajectories
must later be compared. Growing residuals narrow the lease; they do not get
smoothed away to preserve a successful simulation story.

Progression should be staged: software in the loop, hardware in the loop,
bounded empty-cell trials, isolated low-energy hardware, controlled
interaction, and only then the intended operating envelope. Passing one stage
does not transfer evidence to the next. It identifies which assumptions may now
be tested under a slightly less artificial condition.

## Effect Observation and Recovery

Sending a command is not observing its effect. An actuator acknowledgment is
not proof that the plant moved as intended. Stopping software is not restoring
the physical world.

A complete trace links the authorized action, observation packet, controller
and lease, command, actuator response, measured motion, contact, human or
environmental effects, interlock behavior, stop, stabilization, inspection,
compensation, and remaining residual. The trace needs synchronized identities
and clocks so a later reviewer can join a semantic event back to the raw window
and responsible command.

Physical logs often exist at several levels. Raw telemetry supports replay and
new analyses but costs storage and privacy. Event logs retain contacts, slips,
gate failures, holds, and recoveries but miss events their detectors never
anticipated. Semantic traces are easier to reason over but can rewrite an
ambiguous signal as fact. Skill traces name the active controller and authority
lease but may hide the actual command path. Residual logs preserve prediction
errors, unsafe margins, failed recovery, and unresolved effects but depend on a
competent taxonomy.

No representation should silently replace the others. A bounded raw ring
buffer around anomalies, policy changes, interventions, and random audits can
preserve enough context to challenge the summaries. Retention must still obey
privacy, rights, and security constraints. “Log everything” is neither feasible
nor legitimate.

Recovery is likewise physical and inventory-specific. A stop may prevent the
next command while leaving motion, energy, damage, calibration drift, a moved
object, or human reliance behind. The system may need to stabilize, isolate
energy, inspect, compensate, invalidate descendants, and requalify the plant
before operation resumes. Loading the old controller is only one software step.

## Failure Cases

The most common failure is **truth laundering**: a source-authenticated or
schema-valid report is described as true. Provenance establishes lineage, not
accuracy, calibration, coverage, or correct interpretation.

**Agreement inflation** counts several reports that share data, models, caches,
clocks, calibration, operators, or environmental causes as independent votes.
The apparent evidence grows while the causal information does not.

**Disagreement erasure** averages a rare but decisive warning into a confident
fused output. The consumer receives one convenient answer and loses the fact
that a channel contradicted it.

**Freshness laundering** replays an old observation after the sensor, model,
environment, dependency, or consumer changed. A valid past report retains
authority after its basis expired.

**Coverage laundering** treats a clear measurement of one region or population
as evidence about an occluded or missing one. Missingness becomes invisible
rather than an observation result.

**Active-sensing overreach** uses uncertainty to justify more cameras, queries,
movement, credentials, data access, energy, or human attention than the
decision warrants. Perception gains authority by claiming it needs one more
look.

**Deadline blindness** admits a command from a state estimate that was adequate
when computed but stale when acted upon. Average latency hides the tail in
which the safety margin disappears.

**Fallback common mode** gives the advanced and baseline controllers different
names while they share the sensor, estimator, power, runtime, or generated
code that failed. Switching preserves the defect.

**Simulation promotion** treats performance in a modeled plant as hardware or
human-proximity evidence. Omitted contact, latency, wear, or behavior becomes
an unrecorded transfer assumption.

**Software-only recovery** restores a process and closes the incident while
physical state, residual energy, damaged equipment, environmental change, or
human effect remains unresolved.

Each failure is a substitution: lineage for truth, count for independence,
fusion for agreement, a timestamp for freshness, simulation for reality, or a
stop command for recovery. The architecture earns its cost only if it makes
those substitutions harder in real decisions.

## The Strongest Simpler Baseline

A competent perception and control system can be built without a universal
observation ledger. Sensor drivers already carry timestamps and calibration.
Robotics systems fuse state estimates, monitor deadlines, apply constraints,
switch controllers, log telemetry, and expose emergency stops. Software teams
already invalidate caches, pin artifacts, rerun tests, and compare deployment
digests.

The strongest baseline combines those practices well: task-specific fusion,
standard calibration, robust state estimation, explicit timing analysis, a
conventional controller, independent interlocks, canary deployment, and an
incident process. A larger trust record may add latency and paperwork while
giving false confidence that dependence or physical truth has been captured.

That objection should govern the research program. The proposed fabric should
survive only where it improves calibration, detects contradictions or common
causes, preserves consequential disagreement, reduces unsafe admissions,
chooses valuable active observations, catches deadline loss, improves fallback
and recovery, or makes residual effects easier to own. Those benefits must be
measured with task utility, false refusal, delay, energy, privacy, operator
work, storage, nuisance intervention, wear, and total lifecycle cost.

The record should be thinner where ordinary mechanisms already suffice. A
static repository observation may need identity, source, time, dependency, and
expiry. A physical control packet needs much more. Proportionality is part of
observation trust because the sensing and recording machinery can itself cause
harm.

## What the Current Work Establishes

The technical owners behind this unit have exact but narrow formal results.

The observation model contains thirty-two Lean theorem declarations. Its
independent consumer checks seven trace splits, forty-six exact-state lifecycle
mutations, thirteen pair-classification controls, six terminal event kinds, and
twelve same-summary/opposite-common-cause cases. These results establish
behavior of authored finite records: correlated agreement is not promoted as
independent, disagreement is retained, invalidated state is terminal, rejected
events preserve modeled state, and pair labels cannot universally identify a
larger common cause.

The physical-control model contains forty-one Lean declarations across a
finite lease admission model and simulation-trial lifecycle. The independent
consumer rejects thirteen admission-axis mutations and 105 lifecycle
mutations, checks timing and stopping-margin monotonicity, and preserves exact
identity, receipt, stop, support, and external-effect boundaries through its
authored trace.

The numbers matter only inside those models. Every channel, calibration,
dependence root, plant, estimator, safe envelope, timing bound, fallback, and
effect field is authored. No multimodal campaign, natural consequential
workload, physical plant trial, deadline test, stop-path test, sim-to-hardware
transfer, human-proximity study, or independent safety campaign has run here.
The models establish neither environmental truth, calibration, causal
independence, useful fusion, physical safety, recovery, nor deployment
readiness. Both core claims remain at `argument`.

## From a Minimum Contract to an Observation Fabric

The minimum honest implementation starts with two or three channels and one
decision. For the repository case, use immutable file, clean-build test, and
deployment observations. Record exact identity, clock, source, cache and build
dependencies, per-channel hypotheses, disagreement, freshness, consumer, and
expiry. Seed one stale cache, one missing channel, one benign disagreement, and
one spoofed or substituted identity. Reject majority voting when the apparent
votes share a cause.

For physical control, begin in a low-energy simulator with one conventional
controller, one advanced controller, an independent monitor, and a reachable
stop. Seed stale state, latency, estimator error, actuator saturation,
communication loss, and unavailable fallback. Keep every failed task, nuisance
intervention, missed deadline, recovery attempt, and irreversible residual in
the denominator. Hardware transfer waits for positive controls and a separate
authority decision.

The mature target is a substrate-neutral observation fabric spanning digital
reports, cameras, audio, depth, thermal, inertial sensing, scientific
instruments, and future modalities behind stable contracts. It estimates
evidence dependence, chooses observations by expected decision value,
preserves plural hypotheses, invalidates descendants after material change,
and transfers calibrated uncertainty into world models and controllers without
claiming open-world truth.

Its physical-control counterpart hosts classical, learned,
model-predictive, and hybrid controllers behind plant-specific leases while
keeping high-rate safety local and independently enforceable. It predicts when
fallback is becoming unreachable, coordinates active perception with remaining
margin, reconciles commanded and observed effects, and distinguishes stopping,
stabilization, compensation, repair, and irreversible residuals.

This mature system remains a research target. It must be compared against
competent unimodal and multimodal fusion, ordinary robust estimation,
conventional control, constraint filters, switching architectures, and the
best standard engineering process under matched tasks and resources. Simpler
systems that deliver equal calibration, contradiction detection, latency,
fallback, and recovery at lower cost should replace the extra machinery.

## The Strongest Objection

Provenance fields cannot guarantee independence, calibration, or physical
truth. They may merely document correlated error in exquisite detail.

That is correct. A dependence graph can omit the common cause. A calibration
record can be stale or fraudulent. A safe envelope can model the wrong plant.
An independent monitor can share a hidden dependency. A complete receipt can
faithfully describe a bad decision.

The architecture must therefore avoid presenting record completeness as
reality grounding. Records create challenge points. They let another evaluator
ask whether two channels really differ, whether clocks align, whether coverage
matches the consumer, whether the fallback remains reachable, and whether the
observed effect agrees with the command. They make assumptions visible enough
to test and invalidate. They do not make the assumptions true.

If the machinery does not improve downstream decisions, the answer is not a
larger schema. It is a thinner system or a different sensing and control
design.

## Evidence That Would Change the Conclusion

Simpler fusion and control systems with equal calibration, contradiction
detection, selective risk, latency, task value, fallback availability,
recovery, privacy, and cost would justify removing much of the trust model. The
proposal should narrow if active observation rarely changes decisions, if
independence records fail to predict correlated error, if uncertainty packets
are ignored downstream, or if safe holds and fallbacks are unavailable when
needed.

Positive evidence would require natural and synthetic corruptions, missing
channels, time and pose faults, common-cause failures, benign near-neighbors,
positive controls, complete denominators, and independently owned ground truth.
The physical lane would require measured plants, schedulers, actuators,
fallbacks, stop paths, effects, and recovery traces, progressing from
simulation to isolated low-energy hardware without implying human-proximity
authority.

The joint outcome must include useful decisions and safe effects, not only
record validity. A system that always abstains may avoid some errors while
failing its purpose. A system that acts quickly may gain utility while hiding
rare harm. Calibration, decision value, false admission, false refusal,
deadline behavior, physical margin, residual harm, energy, privacy, operator
burden, and lifecycle cost must remain visible together.

## What This Establishes

Observation is not the passive front end of intelligence. It is a governed
transition from signals and reports into bounded evidence that another layer
may use.

The file-system monitor, test runner, reviewer, and deployment probe do not
become four votes merely because four messages arrived. Their identities,
times, targets, transformations, dependencies, coverage, disagreement, and
freshness determine what can be inferred. When evidence is insufficient, the
system asks for a better observation or narrows the action. It does not promote
uncertainty into truth because a decision is waiting.

Physical control makes the same principle urgent. The admissibility of a
command depends on current state, observation age, latency, plant envelope,
actuator limits, stopping margin, human presence, and an independently
reachable fallback. The same symbolic action can become invalid one tick later.
Stopping software is not physical recovery, and a simulation is not the plant.

This discipline does not guarantee reality. It preserves the path by which a
claim about reality was formed and the conditions under which that claim may be
used. That is enough to make contradiction, decay, common causes, and failed
effects governable rather than invisible.

The next unit takes these bounded observations and asks how a system organizes
them into predictions, causal alternatives, and revisable beliefs without
confusing a plausible internal world with the world itself.
